title: Product launches in numbers
heading: How far off is your gut?
intro: Eight real numbers about launching new products: apps, games, gadgets and snacks, and what it takes to get noticed in the first days.
Every figure is real and sourced. Bet on how sure you are, not just on what you think.

outro.heading: Launch day is only the start.
paras: Some of these launches were far bigger than almost anyone guessed; others cost far more to get noticed than people expect.
What a launch has to get right depends on the product, the market and the moment. Keep that in mind today.

questions.q: In July 2023 Meta launched Threads, a rival to Twitter (now X). How long did it take to reach 100 million sign-ups?
questions.sub: the fastest app ever to 100 million at the time
questions.explain: Threads passed 100 million sign-ups within about five days of its 5 July launch, far faster than ChatGPT, which took about two months. It helped that people could join straight from their Instagram account.

questions.q: Nintendo's Switch 2 games console went on sale on 5 June 2025. How many did Nintendo sell in the first four days?
questions.explain: More than 3.5 million units in four days: Nintendo's best start ever, and reportedly the biggest launch of any console. Demand had built for years: the original Switch, launched in 2017, sold over 150 million.
questions.source: Nintendo, June 2025 (via Video Games Chronicle and CNN, 11 June 2025)

questions.q: A 30-second advert during the US Super Bowl is the most expensive slot on television. Roughly what did NBC charge for one in February 2026?
questions.sub: NBC said a handful of slots sold for over $10m
questions.explain: NBC sold 30-second slots at an average of about $8 million, and its ad chief said a handful went for more than $10 million. Brands pay it because the game still draws one of the biggest live audiences in the US, and the adverts themselves become news.
questions.source: Financial Times, via TVLine, February 2026; Sportico, 2025

questions.q: Stanley has made vacuum flasks since 1913. Its sales were $73 million in 2019. After its Quencher cup went viral on social media, what were they in 2023?
questions.sub: about ten times 2019 (a projection reported by CNBC)
questions.explain: A projected $750 million or more. The Quencher had been on sale since 2016; it took off when influencers, and later a viral video of one surviving a car fire, turned a cup into a status object.

questions.q: Grand Theft Auto V, made mainly by Rockstar North in Edinburgh, went on sale in September 2013. How long did it take to earn $1 billion?
questions.explain: Three days: faster than any film, book or game before it. More than a decade later it has sold over 200 million copies, and Edinburgh is one of the centres of the UK games industry.
questions.source: Guinness World Records, Oct 2013; Take-Two Interactive results

questions.q: Apple's Vision Pro headset went on sale in the US in February 2024. What was its starting price?
questions.sub: seven times the price of Meta's Quest 3
questions.explain: It started at $3,499, against $499 for Meta's Quest 3 headset. Apple has not published sales figures for it.
questions.source: Apple, announcement of 8 January 2024 (reported by CNBC)

questions.q: In November 2024 Lindt launched its own 'Dubai chocolate' (pistachio cream and crispy pastry) in Germany, after the trend went viral on TikTok. What did one bar cost at first?
questions.explain: About €14.99 a bar, and the first batch was only 1,000 numbered bars, sold first in its Düsseldorf shop. Queues formed anyway, and supermarket copies soon followed.

questions.q: Josh Wardle made Wordle for his partner and released it to the public in October 2021. In January 2022 The New York Times bought it. For how much?
questions.explain: The Times said only that the price was in the low seven figures. On 1 November 2021 just 90 people had played; by late January millions were playing, almost all through word of mouth.
questions.source: The New York Times / CNBC, 31 January 2022
